about: Round 34: chart labels and 100% stacks as both phones write them (DataGraphics.labelText, normalised / normalisedStack, the chart JSON). labels: a part's label for a chart of kind with its labelAs, decimals and prefix (absent: none set), its value and its share of its whole (0...1). Only a part-to-whole kind (pie, donut, funnel, pictogram, the stacked kinds) says anything but its value; one with no labelAs says its kind's own - a pie's or donut's share, as it always did, every other kind's value. A share is shareText: a whole percentage, halves away from zero, or to the decimals. Both is the value, a space and the share in brackets. A stack's segment's share is of the stack's values above 0. normalised: a 100% stack's values, each over the sum of those above 0, times 100; a value at or below 0 is 0, and a stack with nothing above 0 is all 0. json: the labelAs and legendAt a chart writes (null: not written) - labelAs only when it is not its kind's own, legendAt only when it is not bottom. Drawn, a 100% stack labels each segment in itself (its value, its share or both, as labelAs says) where it is at least 1.25 labels tall (a column's) or 3 labels long (a bar's), never a total above the stack and no strip kept for one, and its scale 0% to 100% at quarters - up the left in 2.5 labels' width for columns, along the foot in a 1.6 labels' strip for bars - with gridlines always on; a stacked chart whose labelAs is percent or both does the same in its segments. A pie's or donut's label with both is 6 labels wide, a pictogram's value column with both 6 labels (else 4).
